title.zh: 卷九十七 晉書23: 列傳12 范延光 張從賓 張延播 楊光遠 廬文進 李金全
title.en: Volume 97 Book of Later Jin 23: Biographies 12 - Fan Yanguang, Zhang Congbin, Zhang Yanbo, Yang Guangyuan, Lu Wenjin, Li Jinquan
title.raw: 卷九十七 晉書23: 列傳12 范延光 張從賓 張延播 楊光遠 廬文進 李金全 Volume 97 Book of Later Jin 23: Biographies 12 - Fan Yanguang, Zhang Congbin, Zhang Yanbo, Yang Guangyuan, Lu Wenjin, Li Jinquan

sentences.zh: 範延光，字子環，鄴郡臨漳人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang, style name Zihuan, was a man of Linzhang in Ye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, whose style name was Zihuan, was a native of Linzhang in Ye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少隸於郡牙，唐明宗牧相州，收為親校。

translations.literal: In youth he served under the commandery military commissioner; when Tang Emperor Mingzong governed Xiangzhou, he was taken in as a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served under the commandery's military commissioner; when Emperor Mingzong of Tang governed Xiangzhou, he was recruited as a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 同光中，明宗下鄆州，梁兵屯楊劉口以扼之，先鋒將康延孝潛使人送款於明宗。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era, Mingzong advanced on Yanzhou; Liang troops encamped at Yangliukou to block him, and the vanguard general Kang Yanxiao secretly sent envoys to offer submission to Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era, Mingzong marched on Yanzhou; Liang forces encamped at Yangliukou to block his advance, while the vanguard general Kang Yanxiao secretly sent envoys to pledge allegiance to Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗欲使人達機事於莊宗，方難其選，延光請行，遂以蠟書授之。

translations.literal: Mingzong wished to send someone to convey confidential matters to Emperor Zhuangzong and was having difficulty choosing whom; Yanguang volunteered to go and was entrusted with a wax-sealed letter.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong wanted to send someone to relay confidential intelligence to Emperor Zhuangzong and was at a loss for whom to choose; Yanguang offered to go and was given a wax-sealed dispatch.

sentences.zh: 延光既至，奏莊宗曰：「楊劉渡控扼已定，未可圖也。

translations.literal: When Yanguang arrived, he reported to Emperor Zhuangzong: "The Yangliu crossing choke-point is already secured and cannot yet be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanguang arrived, he reported to Emperor Zhuangzong: "The Yangliu crossing is already firmly held; it cannot be taken for now.

sentences.zh: 請築壘馬家口，以通汶陽之路。

translations.literal: Please build fortifications at Majiakou to open a route to Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we build fortifications at Majiakou to open a path to Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗從之，復遣歸鄆州。

translations.literal: " Emperor Zhuangzong agreed and sent him back to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong assented and sent him back to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而梁將王彥章攻馬家口所築新壘，明宗恐城中不備，又遣間行告莊宗，請益兵。

translations.literal: Before long the Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked the newly built fort at Majiakou; Mingzong feared the city was unprepared and again sent him by secret route to inform Zhuangzong and request reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked the new fort built at Majiakou; fearing the city was unprepared, Mingzong again sent Yanguang by a secret route to inform Zhuangzong and ask for more troops.

sentences.zh: 中夜至河上，為梁兵所獲，送夷門下獄，榜笞數百，威以白刃，終不泄其事。

translations.literal: At midnight he reached the river and was seized by Liang troops; he was sent to prison below Yimen Gate, flogged hundreds of times, and threatened with naked blades, yet never revealed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the Yellow River at midnight and was captured by Liang troops; they sent him to prison below Yimen Gate, beat him hundreds of strokes with the cudgel, and menaced him with bare blades, yet he never disclosed the mission.

sentences.zh: 復為獄吏所護，在獄半年，不復理問。

translations.literal: He was again protected by the prison officers and spent half a year in jail without further interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The jailers again shielded him, and he remained in prison half a year without being questioned further.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗將至汴城，獄吏即去其桎梏，拜謝而出之，乃見於路側。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was about to reach Bian City, the jailers removed his fetters, bowed in thanks, and released him; he then appeared by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong was about to reach Bian, the jailers at once removed his shackles, bowed in thanks, and released him; he then presented himself by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 莊宗喜，授銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was delighted and appointed him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明宗登極，擢為宣徽使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong ascended the throne, Yanguang was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與霍彥威平青州王公儼，遷檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Together with Huo Yanwei he pacified Qingzhou's Wang Gongyan and was transferred to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Huo Yanwei he pacified Wang Gongyan of Qingzhou and was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 明宗之幸夷門也，至滎陽，聞朱守殷拒命，延光曰：「若不急攻，賊堅矣。

translations.literal: When Mingzong visited Yimen and reached Xingyang, he heard Zhu Shouyin was defying orders; Yanguang said: "If we do not attack urgently, the rebels will have solidified.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong visited Yimen and reached Xingyang, he learned that Zhu Shouyin was defying orders; Yanguang said, "Unless we attack at once, the rebels will dig in.

sentences.zh: 請騎兵五百，臣先赴之，則人心必駭。

translations.literal: Grant me five hundred cavalry; I will go ahead first, and the people's hearts will surely be terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Give me five hundred horsemen and let me go ahead first—the enemy's morale will surely collapse.

sentences.zh: 」明宗從其請。

translations.literal: " Mingzong granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong granted his request.

sentences.zh: 延光自酉時至夜央，馳二百餘里，奄至城下，與賊交鬥。

translations.literal: From the you hour until midnight Yanguang rode over two hundred li, suddenly reached below the walls, and engaged the rebels in battle.
translations.idiomatic: From the you hour until midnight Yanguang galloped more than two hundred li, suddenly appeared below the walls, and fought the rebels hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 翌日，守陴者望見乘輿，乃相率開門，延光先入，與賊巷戰，至厚載門，盡殲其黨，明宗喜之。

translations.literal: The next day the wall defenders saw the imperial carriage and opened the gates in succession; Yanguang entered first, fought the rebels in the alleys to Houzai Gate, and annihilated their party; Mingzong was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the defenders on the walls saw the imperial carriage and opened the gates one after another; Yanguang entered first, fought the rebels street by street to Houzai Gate, and wiped out their band; Mingzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷樞密使，權知鎮州軍府事，尋正授節旄，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, acting administrator of Zhenzhou military government, soon formally granted the commandery standard, and added Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting administrator of the Zhenzhou military government; soon he received the commandery standard in full and was given the additional title Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 長興中，以安重誨得罪，再入為樞密使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era, because An Chonghui fell from favor, he again entered office as Commissioner of Military Affairs and was given the additional title Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era, after An Chonghui fell from grace, Yanguang again became Commissioner of Military Affairs and was made Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 既而以秦王從榮不軌，恐及其禍，屢請外任，明宗久之方許，遂出鎮常山。

translations.literal: Then because Prince of Qin Congrong was disloyal, fearing he would be implicated, he repeatedly requested an outside post; only after a long time did Mingzong consent, and he went out to govern Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Then, when Prince of Qin Congrong turned disloyal, fearing he would be swept up in the disaster, he repeatedly asked for a provincial post; Mingzong only agreed after a long delay, and Yanguang went out to govern Changshan.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，復詔為樞密使，未幾，出為汴州節度使。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era he was again ordered to be Commissioner of Military Affairs; before long he went out as military commissioner of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he was again appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs; before long he was sent out as military commissioner of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 會魏府屯將張令昭逐其帥劉延皓，據城以叛，唐末帝命延光討而平之，遂授鄴都留守，加檢校太師、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the Wei prefecture garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao drove out his commander Liu Yanhao and seized the city in rebellion, Later Tang's final emperor ordered Yanguang to suppress and pacify it; he was then made garrison commander of Ye capital, with the added titles Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei prefecture garrison officer Zhang Lingzhao expelled his commander Liu Yanhao and held the city in revolt, the last emperor of Later Tang ordered Yanguang to suppress him; after victory he was made garrison commander of the Ye capital, with the added titles Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 門下有術士張生者，自雲妙通術數，當延光微時，言將來必為將相，延光既貴，酷信其言。

translations.literal: Among his retainers was a diviner surnamed Zhang who claimed mastery of numerology; when Yanguang was still obscure he said he would surely become a general or minister, and once Yanguang was eminent he deeply believed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Among his household was a diviner named Zhang who claimed to be skilled in numerology; when Yanguang was still obscure, Zhang said he would surely rise to general or minister, and once Yanguang had grown powerful he trusted those words utterly.

sentences.zh: 歷數鎮，嘗館於上舍，延光謂之曰：「余夢大蛇，自臍入腹，半而掣去之，是何祥也？

translations.literal: Through several commanderies he once lodged Zhang in the main guest house; Yanguang said to him: "I dreamed a great serpent entered my belly from the navel and was pulled out halfway—what omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: As he governed several posts he once lodged Zhang in the main guest quarters; Yanguang told him, "I dreamed a great serpent entered my belly through the navel and was pulled out halfway—what omen is that?

sentences.zh: 」張生曰：「蛇者龍也，入腹為帝王之兆明矣。

translations.literal: " Zhang said: "The serpent is the dragon; entering the belly is plainly an omen of becoming emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang said, "The serpent is the dragon; entering the belly is plainly a sign that you will become emperor.

sentences.zh: 」延光自是稍萌僭竊之意。

translations.literal: " From then on Yanguang gradually harbored thoughts of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time Yanguang gradually nursed ambitions of usurpation.

sentences.zh: 及高祖建義於太原，唐末帝遣延光以本部二萬屯遼州，與趙延壽掎角合勢，及延壽兵敗，延光促還，故心不自安。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor raised righteousness at Taiyuan, Later Tang's final emperor sent Yanguang with twenty thousand of his own troops to garrison Liaozhou in pincer coordination with Zhao Yanshou; when Yanshou's army was defeated, Yanguang was urged to return, and his heart was therefore uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Later Jin raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last emperor of Later Tang sent Yanguang with twenty thousand of his own troops to camp at Liaozhou to coordinate with Zhao Yanshou in a pincer; when Yanshou's army was defeated, Yanguang was pressed to withdraw, and he no longer felt secure.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，尋封臨清王，以寬其反側。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor entered Luoyang, he soon enfeoffed him as Prince of Linqing to ease his wavering loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu entered Luoyang, he soon enfeoffed Yanguang as Prince of Linqing to reassure his wavering loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後延光擅殺齊州防禦使秘瓊，而聚兵部下，復收部內刺史入城，高祖甚疑之，乃東幸夷門。

translations.literal: Later Yanguang on his own authority killed Qi prefecture's defense commissioner Mi Qiong, gathered troops under him, and again summoned the prefects within his circuit into the city; the High Ancestor was greatly suspicious and therefore traveled east to Yimen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanguang killed on his own authority Mi Qiong, defense commissioner of Qi prefecture, gathered troops under his command, and again summoned the prefects within his circuit into the city; Gaozu grew deeply suspicious and traveled east to Yimen.

sentences.zh: 時延光有牙校孫銳者，與延光有鄉曲之舊，軍機民政，一以委焉。

translations.literal: At that time Yanguang had a military aide named Sun Rui who had old hometown ties with him; military and civil affairs were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yanguang had a military aide named Sun Rui, an old acquaintance from his home district; he entrusted all military and civil affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 故魏博六州之賦，無半錢上供，符奏之間，有不如意者，銳即對延光毀之，其兇戾也如此。

translations.literal: Thus of the taxes of the six prefectures of Weibo not half a coin was sent up; among memorials and reports, if anything displeased him, Rui would tear it up before Yanguang—his violence was like this.
translations.idiomatic: As a result not half a coin of the taxes from Weibo's six prefectures reached the court; whenever a memorial displeased him, Rui would tear it up in Yanguang's presence—such was his brutish arrogance.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷遣使封延光為臨清王，因會僚屬，延光暴得疾，伏枕經旬，銳乃密惑群小，召澶州刺史馮暉等，以不臣之謀逼於延光，延光亦惑於術者，因而聽之。

translations.literal: At first the court sent envoys to enfeoff Yanguang as Prince of Linqing; when he met his staff he suddenly fell ill and lay on his pillow for ten days; Rui secretly swayed petty men, summoned Cao prefecture's governor Feng Hui and others, and pressed disloyal plans on Yanguang; Yanguang was also deluded by the diviner and therefore assented.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first sent envoys to enfeoff Yanguang as Prince of Linqing, he was meeting his staff when he suddenly fell ill and lay abed for ten days; Rui secretly swayed petty followers, summoned Cao prefecture's governor Feng Hui and others, and pressed a treasonous plot on Yanguang, who was also deluded by the diviner and therefore went along.

sentences.zh: 天福二年夏六月，遣銳與暉將步騎二萬，南抵黎陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Tianfu he sent Rui and Hui to lead twenty thousand foot and horse south to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer in the second year of Tianfu he sent Rui and Hui south with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry as far as Liyang.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：延光以馮暉為都部署，以孫銳為兵馬都監。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Yanguang made Feng Hui overall commander and Sun Rui military overseer.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 states that Yanguang made Feng Hui overall commander and Sun Rui military overseer.)

sentences.zh: 時銳以女妓十餘輩從之，擁蓋操扇，必歌吹而後食，將士煩熱，睹之解體，尋為王師所敗，賊眾退還鄴城。

translations.literal: At that time Rui was accompanied by more than ten female entertainers; holding parasols and wielding fans, he would not eat until there was singing and music; the troops, hot and weary, lost heart at the sight; soon they were defeated by the imperial army and the rebels withdrew to Ye City.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Rui traveled with more than ten female entertainers, borne under parasols while servants fanned him; he would not dine until musicians played; the troops, sweltering and exhausted, lost all fighting spirit at the sight; soon the imperial army defeated them and the rebels fell back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖繼遣楊光遠討之，延光知事不濟，乃殺孫銳以歸其罪，發人賫表待罪，且邀姑息，高祖不許。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor then sent Yang Guangyuan to suppress him; Yanguang knew the affair would not succeed, killed Sun Rui to assign him the blame, sent men bearing a memorial awaiting punishment, and also sought leniency; the High Ancestor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then sent Yang Guangyuan against him; seeing the cause was lost, Yanguang killed Sun Rui to lay the blame on him, dispatched envoys with a memorial submitting to judgment, and also pleaded for mercy; Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 及經歲受圍，城中饑窘，高祖以師老民勞，思解其役，遣謁者入謂之曰：「卿既危蹙，破在旦夕。

translations.literal: After a year under siege the city was hungry and desperate; the High Ancestor, because the army was weary and the people exhausted, wished to end the campaign and sent a chamberlain in to say: "You are already in dire straits; defeat is imminent.
translations.idiomatic: After a year under siege the city was starving and desperate; Gaozu, seeing the army worn down and the people exhausted, wished to end the campaign and sent a chamberlain in to say, "You are already cornered; your fall is only a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 能返掌轉規，改節歸我，我當以大藩處之。

translations.literal: If you can turn your hand and change course, alter your allegiance and return to me, I shall place you in a great frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: If you can turn back, change your allegiance, and submit to me, I will give you a great frontier command.

sentences.zh: 如降而殺之，則何以享國？

translations.literal: If I killed you after you surrendered, how could I enjoy the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If I killed you after you surrendered, how could I hold the realm in honor?

sentences.zh: 明明白日，可質是言。

translations.literal: In broad daylight you may take this as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Under the bright sun you may hold me to this word.

sentences.zh: 」因賜鐵券，改封高平郡王，移鎮太平。

translations.literal: " He therefore granted an iron covenant, changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Gaoping, and transferred him to govern Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted an iron covenant of mercy, changed his title to Prince of Gaoping, and reassigned him to govern Taiping.

sentences.zh: 延光謂門人李式曰：「主上敦信明義，言無不踐，許以不死，則不死矣。

translations.literal: Yanguang said to his retainer Li Shi: "Our lord is sincere in faith and clear in righteousness; his words are never unfulfilled; if he promises you will not die, you will not die.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang told his retainer Li Shi, "Our lord is steadfast in faith and righteous in deed; he never breaks his word; if he promises you will not die, you will not die.

sentences.zh: 」因撤去守備，

translations.literal: " He therefore removed the defenses,
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the defenses dismantled,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：延光猶遷延未決，宣徽南院使劉處讓復入諭之，延光意乃決。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Yanguang still hesitated and had not decided; the Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Attendant's Office Liu Churang entered again to counsel him, and then Yanguang's mind was made up.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that Yanguang still hesitated; Commissioner Liu Churang of the Southern Bureau entered again to persuade him, and only then did Yanguang make up his mind.)

sentences.zh: 素服請降。

translations.literal: He wore plain robes and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He put on plain robes and asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 及赴汶上，逾月入覲。

translations.literal: When he went to Wenshang, after more than a month he entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: After he went to Wenshang, more than a month passed before he presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 尋表請罷免，高祖再三答諭方允，制以延光為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized requesting dismissal; only after the High Ancestor repeatedly answered and instructed did he consent, and by edict Yanguang was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved; only after Gaozu repeatedly reassured him did he agree, and by edict Yanguang was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 居闕下期歲，高祖每召賜飲宴，待之與群臣無間。

translations.literal: He dwelt at the capital nearly a year; the High Ancestor often summoned him to banquets and treated him no differently from the other ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at the capital nearly a year; Gaozu often summoned him to feasts and treated him no differently from the other ministers.

sentences.zh: 一日，從容上奏，願就河陽私邸，以便頤養，高祖許之。

translations.literal: One day he calmly submitted that he wished to go to his private residence at Heyang for ease in nourishing his health; the High Ancestor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: One day he calmly reported that he wished to retire to his private house at Heyang for his health; Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 延光攜妻子輦奇貨從焉，每過郡邑，多為關吏所糾。

translations.literal: Yanguang took his wife and children and loaded rare goods on carts to follow; whenever he passed a commandery or county he was often challenged by barrier officers.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang took his wife and children and carts laden with rare goods; whenever he passed a commandery or county the barrier officers often detained him.

sentences.zh: 時楊光遠居守洛下，兼領孟、懷，既利其財，復漸測朝廷密旨，遂奏云：「延光國之奸臣，若不羈縻，必北出塞，南入吳，請召令西都居止。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Guangyuan was garrisoning Luoyang and also held Meng and Huai; coveting his wealth and gradually discerning the court's secret intent, he memorialized: "Yanguang is a traitor to the state; if not restrained he will surely flee north beyond the passes or south into Wu; I ask that he be summoned to dwell in the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Guangyuan was holding Luoyang and also governed Meng and Huai; coveting Yanguang's wealth and gradually sensing the court's secret intent, he memorialized, "Yanguang is a traitor to the state; unless he is restrained he will flee north beyond the frontier or south into Wu; I ask that he be summoned to reside in the western capital.

sentences.zh: 」高祖允之。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 光遠使其子承勛以兵環其第，逼令自裁。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had his son Chengxun surround his residence with troops and forced him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan had his son Chengxun surround the residence with troops and pressed him to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「明天子在上，賜金書許我不死，爾之父子何得脅制如此？

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "The enlightened Son of Heaven is above and granted a golden writ promising I would not die—how can you father and son coerce me like this?
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said, "The enlightened Son of Heaven sits above and granted me a golden writ promising I would not die—how dare you father and son coerce me like this?

sentences.zh: 」明旦，則以白刃驅之，令上馬之浮橋，排於水中。

translations.literal: " At dawn they drove him with naked blades, made him mount onto the pontoon bridge, and pushed him into the water.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn they drove him at sword point onto the pontoon bridge and pushed him into the river.

sentences.zh: 光遠紿奏云：「延光投河自溺而死。

translations.literal: Guangyuan falsely reported: "Yanguang threw himself into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan falsely reported, "Yanguang threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 」水運軍使曹千獲其屍於郡東繆家灘。

translations.literal: " The water-transport army commissioner Cao Qian recovered his corpse at Miaojia Beach east of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " The water-transport army commissioner Cao Qian recovered his body at Miaojia Beach east of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，輟朝二日，詔許歸葬於鄴，仍贈太師。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor heard it he suspended court for two days, ordered that burial be permitted at Ye, and still posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of it he suspended court for two days, permitted burial at Ye, and still posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 延光初為近臣，及領重鎮，禮賢接士，動皆由禮，故甚獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: At first as a close minister, and when he held a weighty commandery, he honored the worthy and received scholars; his actions were all according to ritual, and he therefore won great praise at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first a close minister and later held a major command, he honored the worthy and received scholars with courtesy; his conduct was always proper, and he won great esteem in his day.

sentences.zh: 洎鎮常山日，以部將梁漢塘獲王都名馬，入罪而取之；

translations.literal: When he governed Changshan, because his subordinate Liang Hantang obtained Wang Du's famous horses, he charged him with a crime and seized them;
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Changshan, his subordinate Liang Hantang had obtained Wang Du's famous horses; Yanguang charged him with a crime and took the horses for himself;

sentences.zh: 在魏州日，以齊州防禦使秘瓊獲董溫琪珠金妓妾，及經其境，復害而奪之。

translations.literal: In his days at Weizhou, because Qi prefecture's defense commissioner Mi Qiong obtained Dong Wenqi's pearls, gold, and female entertainers, when he passed through his territory Yanguang again killed him and seized them.
translations.idiomatic: While at Weizhou, when Qi prefecture's defense commissioner Mi Qiong had obtained Dong Wenqi's pearls, gold, and courtesans, Yanguang killed him when he passed through the territory and seized everything.

sentences.zh: 物議由是減之。

translations.literal: Public opinion therefore diminished him.
translations.idiomatic: Public esteem for him fell accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及懼罪以謀叛，復忍恥以偷生，不能引決，遂至強死，何非夫之甚也！

translations.literal: When he feared punishment and plotted rebellion, then endured shame to cling to life, unable to take resolution, and thus came to forced death—how greatly he failed as a man!
translations.idiomatic: When he feared punishment and rebelled, then endured disgrace to cling to life, unable to take his own life, and was killed by force—how utterly he failed the measure of a man!

sentences.zh: 張從賓，未詳何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Congbin—his place of origin is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Congbin—his place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 始事唐莊宗為小校，從戰有功。

translations.literal: He first served Tang Emperor Zhuangzong as a junior officer and had merit in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang as a junior officer and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，自捧聖指揮使領澄州刺史，遷左右羽林都校。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he rose from commander of the Pingsheng Guard to hold Chen prefecture as governor and was transferred to chief commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era of Tang he rose from commander of the Pingsheng Guard to govern Chen prefecture and was promoted to chief commander of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.

sentences.zh: 從藥彥稠討楊彥溫於河中，平之。

translations.literal: He followed Yao Yanzhou to suppress Yang Yanwen at Hezhong and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yao Yanzhou in suppressing Yang Yanwen at Hezhong and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 長興中，領壽州忠正軍節度使，加檢校太保、侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he held Shou prefecture as military commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army, with the added titles Acting Grand Guardian and overall commander of the Palace Guard infantry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he was military commissioner of Shou prefecture for the Zhongzheng Army, with the added titles Acting Grand Guardian and overall commander of the Palace Guard infantry.

sentences.zh: 從賓素便佞，每進言，明宗多納之。

translations.literal: Congbin was by nature skilled in flattery; whenever he offered advice Mingzong often accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin was naturally skilled at flattery; Mingzong often accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 有供奉官丁延徽者，性貪狡，時奉詔監廩，以犯贓下獄，權貴多為救解，明宗怒，不許。

translations.literal: There was a palace attendant named Ding Yanhui who was greedy and cunning; at the time he was ordered to oversee the granaries and was imprisoned for corruption; many powerful men pleaded for him, but Mingzong was angry and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: There was a palace attendant named Ding Yanhui, greedy and cunning; ordered at the time to oversee the granaries, he was imprisoned for embezzlement; many powerful men interceded for him, but Mingzong was angry and refused.

sentences.zh: 從賓因奏他事，言及延徽，明宗曰：「非但爾言，蘇秦說予，亦不得也。

translations.literal: Congbin, while memorializing on another matter, mentioned Yanhui; Mingzong said: "Even if not only you spoke—if Su Qin persuaded me, it would still not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: While reporting on another matter Congbin mentioned Yanhui; Mingzong said, "Even if not only you spoke—even if Su Qin himself pleaded for him, I would not grant it.

sentences.zh: 」延徽竟就戮。

translations.literal: " Yanhui was finally executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanhui was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 長興末，從賓出鎮靈武，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing, Congbin went out to govern Lingwu and was given the added title Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Changxing era Congbin was sent out to govern Lingwu and was given the added title Acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，受代入覲，會駕東幸，留從賓警巡洛下。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Congbin was relieved and entered audience; as the imperial carriage traveled east he was left to patrol and guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Congbin was relieved and came to court; when the emperor traveled east he was left to patrol Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 一日，逢留司御史於天津橋，從兵百人，不分路而過，排御史於水中，從賓紿奏其酒醉，其兇傲如此。

translations.literal: One day he met the capital duty censor at Tianjin Bridge with a hundred followers; they would not yield the road and pushed the censor into the water; Congbin falsely reported he was drunk—his violence and arrogance were like this.
translations.idiomatic: One day he met the capital duty censor at Tianjin Bridge with a hundred followers; they refused to yield the road and shoved the censor into the water; Congbin falsely reported that the censor was drunk—such was his brutish arrogance.

sentences.zh: 及範延光據鄴城叛，詔從賓為副部署使，從楊光遠同討延光。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang held Ye City in rebellion, Congbin was ordered as deputy overall commander to follow Yang Guangyuan in jointly suppressing Yanguang.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion, Congbin was ordered deputy overall commander to join Yang Guangyuan in suppressing Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 會延光使人誘從賓，從賓時在河陽，乃起兵以應之。

translations.literal: When Yanguang sent men to entice Congbin, Congbin was then at Heyang and raised troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang sent envoys to win Congbin over; Congbin was then at Heyang and raised troops in support.

sentences.zh: 先害皇子重信，及入洛，又害皇子重乂，取內庫金帛以給部伍，因東據汜水關，且欲觀望軍勢。

translations.literal: He first killed the prince Chongxin; when he entered Luoyang he also killed the prince Chongyi, took gold and silk from the inner treasury to supply his troops, then held Sishui Pass in the east and wished to watch how the armies fared.
translations.idiomatic: He first killed Prince Chongxin; after entering Luoyang he also killed Prince Chongyi, seized gold and silk from the inner treasury to pay his troops, then seized Sishui Pass to the east and waited to see how the fighting would go.

sentences.zh: 高祖命杜重威、侯益分兵討之，從賓大敗，乘馬入河，溺水而死焉。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor ordered Du Chongwei and Hou Yi to divide forces and suppress him; Congbin was greatly defeated, rode his horse into the river, and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Du Chongwei and Hou Yi to attack him with divided forces; Congbin was routed, rode into the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠，小字阿檀，及長，止名檀，唐天成中，以明宗改御名為亶，以偏傍字犯之，始改名光遠，字德明，其先沙陀部人也。

translations.literal: Yang Guangyuan, childhood name Atan; when grown he used only the name Tan; in the Tiancheng era of Tang, because Mingzong changed his imperial name to Dan and the component characters were tabooed, he first changed his name to Guangyuan, style name Deming; his ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangyuan's childhood name was Atan; when he grew up he used only Tan; during the Tiancheng era of Tang, when Mingzong changed his imperial name to Dan and the component characters became taboo, he renamed himself Guangyuan, style name Deming; his forebears were Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 父阿噔啜，後改名瑊，事唐武皇為隊長。

translations.literal: His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Tang's Martial Emperor as a squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: His father Adengchuo later renamed himself Jian and served Tang's Martial Emperor as a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 光遠事莊宗為騎將，唐天祐中，莊宗遣振武節度使周德威討劉守光於幽州，因令光遠隸於德威麾下。

translations.literal: Guangyuan served Zhuangzong as a cavalry officer; in the Tianyou era of Tang, Zhuangzong sent Zhenwu military commissioner Zhou Dewei to suppress Liu Shouguang at Youzhou and therefore placed Guangyuan under Dewei's command.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan served Zhuangzong as a cavalry officer; in the Tianyou era Zhuangzong sent Zhenwu military commissioner Zhou Dewei against Liu Shouguang at Youzhou and placed Guangyuan under Dewei.

sentences.zh: 後與德威拒契丹於新州，一軍以深入致敗，因傷其臂，遂廢，罷於家。

translations.literal: Later with Dewei he resisted the Khitans at Xinzhou; the army was defeated for advancing too deep, his arm was wounded, he was disabled, and dismissed to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Dewei fought the Khitans at Xinzhou; the army was defeated after advancing too far, Guangyuan's arm was wounded, he was disabled, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，思其戰功，命為幽州馬步軍都指揮使、檢校尚書右僕射，戍瓦橋關久之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he recalled his battle merit and appointed him overall commander of Youzhou horse and foot, Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat of the Right, garrisoning Waqiao Pass for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne he remembered his service and appointed him overall commander of Youzhou horse and foot and Acting Vice Director of the Right Secretariat, and he garrisoned Waqiao Pass for many years.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，歷媯、瀛、易、冀四州刺史。

translations.literal: In Mingzong's reign he successively held the four prefectures of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he served in turn as governor of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji prefectures.

sentences.zh: 光遠雖不識字，然有口辯，通於吏理，在郡有政聲，明宗頗重之。

translations.literal: Although Guangyuan could not read, he was eloquent and understood administrative principles; in the prefectures he had a reputation for good government, and Mingzong valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Although illiterate, Guangyuan was eloquent and skilled in administration; his prefectures won praise for good government, and Mingzong held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 長興中，契丹有中山之敗，生擒其將紮拉等數十人，送於闕下，其後契丹既通和，遣使乞歸之，明宗與大臣謀議，特放還蕃。

translations.literal: In Changxing the Khitans suffered defeat at Zhongshan; dozens including their general Zhala were captured alive and sent to court; later when the Khitans had made peace they sent envoys asking their return; Mingzong consulted ministers and specially ordered them released back to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing the Khitans were defeated at Zhongshan; dozens of captives including their general Zhala were sent to court; after peace the Khitans asked for their return; Mingzong consulted his ministers and ordered them released to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 一日，召光遠於便殿言其事，光遠曰：「紮拉等北土之善戰者，彼失之如喪手足；

translations.literal: One day he summoned Guangyuan to the informal hall to discuss the matter; Guangyuan said: "Zhala and the others are the northland's best fighters; for them to lose them is like losing hands and feet;
translations.idiomatic: One day Mingzong summoned Guangyuan to the informal hall to discuss it; Guangyuan said, "Zhala and the others are the Khitans' best fighters; to lose them is like losing hands and feet;

sentences.zh: 又在此累年，備諳中國事，若放還非便。

translations.literal: moreover they have been here many years and are thoroughly versed in Middle Kingdom affairs—if released it would not be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: moreover they have been here for years and know our affairs inside out—it would not be wise to send them back.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「蕃人重盟誓，既通歡好，必不相負。

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "The barbarians value sworn covenants; now that we are on friendly terms they surely will not betray us.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said, "The Khitans honor their oaths; now that we are at peace they will not betray us.

sentences.zh: 」光遠曰：「臣恐後悔不及也。

translations.literal: " Guangyuan said: "Your servant fears you will regret it too late.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangyuan said, "I fear Your Majesty will regret it when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 」明宗遂止，深嘉其抗直。

translations.literal: " Mingzong therefore stopped and deeply praised his forthright resistance.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong held back and deeply praised his blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 後自振武節度使移鎮中山，累加檢校太傅，將兵戍蔚州。

translations.literal: Later he moved from Zhenwu military commissioner to govern Zhongshan, was repeatedly given Acting Grand Tutor, and led troops to garrison You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved from Zhenwu military commissioner to Zhongshan, was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Tutor, and led troops garrisoning You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉義於太原，唐末帝遣光遠與張敬達屯兵於城下，俄而契丹大至，為其所敗，圍其寨久之，軍中糧絕，光遠乃與次將安審琦等殺敬達，擁眾歸命。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor raised righteousness at Taiyuan, Later Tang's final emperor sent Guangyuan and Zhang Jingda to encamp below the city; soon the Khitans arrived in force, defeated them, and besieged their camp a long time until provisions were exhausted; Guangyuan then with the second commander An Shenqi and others killed Jingda and led the masses to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, the last emperor of Later Tang sent Guangyuan and Zhang Jingda to camp below the city; the Khitans soon arrived in force, defeated them, and besieged their camp until food ran out; Guangyuan then joined the second-in-command An Shenqi and others in killing Jingda and leading the army to surrender.

sentences.zh: 從高祖入洛，加檢校太尉，充宣武軍節度使、同平章事，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: Following the High Ancestor into Luoyang he was given Acting Grand Commandant, made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and Associate Grand Councilor, and assigned to judge the affairs of the Six Armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gaozu into Luoyang, was made Acting Grand Commandant, military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army and Associate Grand Councilor, and placed in charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 是時，光遠每對高祖，常悒然不樂，高祖慮有不足，密遣近臣訊之。

translations.literal: At that time whenever Guangyuan faced the High Ancestor he was often gloomy and displeased; the High Ancestor feared something was lacking and secretly sent a close minister to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guangyuan often looked gloomy in Gaozu's presence; Gaozu feared he was dissatisfied and secretly sent a close minister to ask why.

sentences.zh: 光遠附奏曰：「臣貴為將相，非有不足，但以張生鐵死得其所，臣弗如也，衷心內愧，是以不樂。

translations.literal: Guangyuan appended a memorial saying: "Your servant is honored as general and minister and lacks nothing; yet Zhang ShengTie died in the right place — I cannot match him. My heart is inwardly ashamed, and therefore I am not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan added a memorial saying, "I stand honored as general and minister and want for nothing; yet Zhang Raw Iron died as he should, and I am not his equal. I am ashamed at heart, and that is why I am unhappy.

sentences.zh: 」生鐵，蓋敬達之小字也。

translations.literal: " ShengTie was Jingda's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " ShengTie — "raw iron" — was Zhang Jingda's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞其言，以光遠為忠純之最者也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor heard his words and considered Guangyuan the most loyal and pure of men.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard this and judged Guangyuan the most loyal and upright of all.

sentences.zh: 其實光遠故為其言，以邀高祖之重信也。

translations.literal: In fact Guangyuan had deliberately spoken thus to win the High Ancestor's deep trust.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Guangyuan had said this on purpose to win Gaozu's deepest trust.

sentences.zh: 明年，範延光據鄴城叛，高祖命光遠率師討之。

translations.literal: The next year Fan Yanguang seized Ye city and rebelled; the High Ancestor ordered Guangyuan to lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Fan Yanguang seized Ye city and rebelled; Gaozu ordered Guangyuan to lead an army against him.

sentences.zh: 將濟河，會滑州軍亂，時軍眾欲推光遠為主。

translations.literal: About to cross the river, there was a mutiny in the army at Huazhou, and the troops wished to make Guangyuan their leader.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the river, the army at Huazhou mutinied, and the troops wanted to make Guangyuan their leader.

sentences.zh: 光遠曰：「自古有折臂天子乎？

translations.literal: Guangyuan said: "Since antiquity has there ever been an emperor with a broken arm?
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan said, "Has there ever in history been an emperor with a broken arm?

sentences.zh: 且天子豈公輩販弄之物？

translations.literal: Moreover, is the Son of Heaven some thing for you fellows to peddle and manipulate?
translations.idiomatic: And is the Son of Heaven some trinket for the likes of you to bandy about?

sentences.zh: 晉陽之降，乃勢所窮迫，今若為之，直反賊也。

translations.literal: The surrender at Jinyang was forced by dire circumstances; if I did this now, I would be nothing but a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Our surrender at Jinyang was forced by desperate circumstances; to do this now would make me nothing but a rebel.

sentences.zh: 」由是其下惕然，無復言者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon his subordinates were awed and no one spoke again.
translations.idiomatic: " His men were shaken into silence, and no one spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，尤加寵重。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor heard of it and favored him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of this, he favored Guangyuan all the more.

sentences.zh: 光遠既圍延光，尋授魏博行府節度使。

translations.literal: Once Guangyuan had besieged Yanguang, he was soon made provisional military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangyuan besieged Yanguang, he was soon made provisional military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 兵柄在手，以為高祖懼己，稍干預朝政，或抗有所奏，高祖亦曲從之。

translations.literal: With military power in hand, he believed the High Ancestor feared him; he gradually intervened in court affairs, and when he obstinately submitted opinions, the High Ancestor also indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: With the army in his hands, he believed Gaozu feared him; he began meddling in court affairs, and when he stubbornly pressed his views, Gaozu indulged him.

sentences.zh: 復下詔以其子承祚尚長安公主，次子承信皆授美官。

translations.literal: An edict further had his son Chengzuo marry Princess Chang'an and his second son Chengxin both given fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further had his son Chengzuo marry Princess Chang'an and gave his second son Chengxin distinguished offices.

sentences.zh: 恩渥殊等，為當時之冠。

translations.literal: Favor unmatched, the foremost of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His favor was unmatched, the greatest of the day.

sentences.zh: 桑維翰為樞密使，往往彈射其事，光遠心銜之。

translations.literal: Sang Weihan was Commissioner of Military Affairs and often impeached him on these matters; Guangyuan bore resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan, as Commissioner of Military Affairs, often attacked him on these matters, and Guangyuan nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及延光降，光遠入朝，面奏維翰擅權。

translations.literal: When Yanguang surrendered, Guangyuan came to court and personally memorialized that Weihan monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang surrendered, Guangyuan came to court and accused Weihan face to face of monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 高祖以光遠方有功於國，乃出維翰鎮相州，光遠為西京留守，兼鎮河陽，因罷其兵權。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, because Guangyuan had recently rendered great service to the state, sent Weihan out to govern Xiangzhou, made Guangyuan defender of the Western Capital and concurrently military commissioner of Heyang, thereby removing his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangyuan had just rendered great service, Gaozu sent Weihan out to govern Xiangzhou, made Guangyuan defender of the Western Capital and concurrently military commissioner of Heyang, and thereby stripped him of military command.

sentences.zh: 光遠由此怨望，潛貯異志，多以珍玩奉契丹，訴己之屈，又私養部曲千餘人，撓法犯禁，河、洛之人，恒如備盜。

translations.literal: From this Guangyuan nursed resentment, secretly harbored divergent ambitions, often sent precious curios to the Khitans complaining of his grievances, and privately maintained over a thousand retainers, disturbing the law and violating prohibitions — the people of the Yellow River and Luoyang regions always lived as if guarding against robbers.
translations.idiomatic: From this Guangyuan turned resentful, secretly harbored other ambitions, often sent precious curios to the Khitans to plead his grievances, and privately kept more than a thousand retainers who flouted the law; the people of the Yellow River region and Luoyang lived in constant fear, as if guarding against bandits.

sentences.zh: 尋冊拜太尉、兼中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he was invested as Grand Commandant and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was invested as Grand Commandant and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時範延光致仕，輦囊裝妓妾，居於河陽。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Yanguang had retired, loading carts with concubines and courtesans, and lived at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fan Yanguang had retired, loading carts with concubines and courtesans, and was living at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 光遠利其奇貨，且慮為子孫之讎，因奏延光不家汴、洛，出舍外藩，非南走淮夷，則北走契丹，宜早除之。

translations.literal: Guangyuan coveted his rare goods and also feared he would become an enemy to his descendants; he therefore memorialized that Yanguang, not residing in Bian or Luoyang but lodging in an outer province, would either flee south to the Huai barbarians or north to the Khitans, and should be removed early.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan coveted his wealth and also feared he would become an enemy to his descendants; he memorialized that Yanguang, not living in Bian or Luoyang but staying in an outer province, would either flee south to the Huai tribes or north to the Khitans, and should be eliminated at once.

sentences.zh: 高祖以許之不死，鐵券在焉，持疑未允。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, because he had promised him he would not die and the iron certificate was still in effect, hesitated and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, having promised that Yanguang would not be put to death and with the iron certificate still in force, hesitated and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 光遠乃遣子承勛以甲士圍其第，逼令自裁。

translations.literal: Guangyuan then sent his son Chengxun with armored soldiers to surround his residence and forced him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan then sent his son Chengxun with armored troops to surround Yanguang's residence and forced him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「天子在上，安得如此！

translations.literal: Yanguang said: "The Son of Heaven is above — how can you do this!
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said, "The Son of Heaven is above — how dare you do this!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使者乞移居洛下，行及河橋，擯於流而溺殺之，矯奏雲延光自投河，朝廷以適會其意，弗之理。

translations.literal: " He then sent an envoy begging to move to Luoyang; when he reached the river bridge they shoved him into the current and drowned him, falsely reporting that Yanguang had thrown himself into the river — the court, as this suited their wishes, paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent an envoy begging to move to Luoyang; when he reached the river bridge they shoved him into the current and drowned him, falsely reporting that Yanguang had thrown himself into the river. The court, pleased that this suited their purpose, paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 後逾歲入覲，高祖為置曲宴，教坊伶人以光遠暴斂重賦，因陳戲譏之，光遠殊無慚色。

translations.literal: More than a year later when he came to court for an audience, the High Ancestor held a banquet with music; entertainers from the Music Office satirized Guangyuan's harsh levies and heavy taxes in performance, yet Guangyuan showed not the least shame.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, when he came to court, Gaozu held a banquet with music; entertainers from the Music Office satirized Guangyuan's harsh levies and heavy taxes in a skit, yet Guangyuan showed not the slightest shame.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂光遠曰：「元城之役，卿左右皆立功，未曾旌賞，今各與一郡，俾厘任以榮之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said to Guangyuan: "At the Yuancheng campaign, your close followers all rendered merit yet were never rewarded; now each shall receive a prefecture, that they may take office and be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said to Guangyuan, "At the Yuancheng campaign your close followers all rendered service yet were never rewarded; now each shall receive a prefecture, that they may take office and be honored.

sentences.zh: 」因命為刺史者凡數人。

translations.literal: " He then appointed several as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed several of them prefect.

sentences.zh: 時王建立自青州移鎮上黨，乃以光遠為平盧軍節度使，封東平王。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jianli moved from Qingzhou to govern Shangdang; Guangyuan was made military commissioner of the Pinglu Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jianli moved from Qingzhou to govern Shangdang, Guangyuan was made military commissioner of the Pinglu Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 光遠面奏，請與長子同行，尋授承勛萊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Guangyuan memorialized in person, asking to travel with his eldest son; Chengxun was soon made defense commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan memorialized in person asking to travel with his eldest son; Chengxun was soon made defense commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 及赴任，仆從妓妾至千餘騎，滿盈僭侈，為方嶽之最。

translations.literal: When he took up his post, retainers and courtesans numbered over a thousand riders — overflowing display and imperious extravagance, the utmost among regional lords.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post, retainers and courtesans numbered more than a thousand mounted followers — display so lavish and arrogance so great that no regional lord surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 下車之後，惟以刻剝為事。

translations.literal: After arriving to govern, he devoted himself solely to extortion.
translations.idiomatic: After he took office, he devoted himself solely to extortion.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，冊拜太師，封壽王。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Guangyuan was invested as Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, Guangyuan was invested as Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·馬仁鎬傳》：晉天福中，青州楊光遠將圖不軌，以仁鎬為節度副使，伺其動靜。

translations.literal: (Song History, biography of Ma Rendegao: In Later Jin's Tianfu era, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was plotting sedition; Rendegao was made deputy military commissioner to watch his movements.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History, biography of Ma Rendegao, records that in the Tianfu era of Later Jin, Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was plotting rebellion and Rendegao was made deputy military commissioner to watch his movements.

sentences.zh: 歷二年，或譖仁鎬於朝，改護國軍行軍司馬。

translations.literal: After two years someone slandered Rendegao at court; he was transferred to army marshal of the Huguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: After two years someone slandered Rendegao at court, and he was transferred to army marshal of the Huguo Army.

sentences.zh: 仁鎬至河中數月，光遠反書聞。）〉

translations.literal: When Rendegao had been at Hezhong several months, word of Guangyuan's rebellion arrived.)
translations.idiomatic: When Rendegao had been at Hezhong several months, word of Guangyuan's rebellion arrived.)

sentences.zh: 後因景延廣上言，請取光遠麾下所借官馬二百匹，光遠怒曰：「此馬先帝賜我，何以復取？

translations.literal: Later, because Jing Yanguang proposed reclaiming two hundred government horses lent to Guangyuan's command, Guangyuan angrily said: "These horses the former emperor gave me — why take them back?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jing Yanguang proposed reclaiming two hundred government horses lent to Guangyuan's command, Guangyuan angrily said, "These horses the former emperor gave me — why take them back?

sentences.zh: 是疑我也。

translations.literal: You distrust me.
translations.idiomatic: This means you distrust me.

sentences.zh: 」遂遣人潛召取子承祚自單州奔歸，朝廷乃就除淄州刺史，以從其便。

translations.literal: " He then secretly sent men to summon his son Chengzuo back from Shan prefecture; the court thereupon appointed Chengzuo prefect of Zi to accommodate him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then secretly sent men to summon his son Chengzuo back from Shan prefecture; the court thereupon appointed Chengzuo prefect of Zi to suit his convenience.

sentences.zh: 光遠益驕，因此構契丹，述少帝違好之短，且言大饑之後，國用空虛，此時一舉可以平定。

translations.literal: Guangyuan grew all the more arrogant; he therefore incited the Khitans, recounting the Last Emperor's breaches of the good relations, and saying that after the great famine the state's coffers were empty — at this moment one stroke could pacify all.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan grew all the more arrogant; he therefore incited the Khitans, recounting the Last Emperor's breaches of the alliance and saying that after the great famine the treasury was empty — one stroke now could settle everything.

sentences.zh: 開運元年正月，契丹南牧，陷我博陵，少帝幸澶淵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitans drove south, seized our Boling, and the Last Emperor went to Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Kaiyun, the Khitans drove south, seized Boling, and the Last Emperor went to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 三月，契丹退，命李守貞、符彥卿率師東討。

translations.literal: In the third month, when the Khitans withdrew, he ordered Li Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing to lead troops east to suppress Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, after the Khitans withdrew, he ordered Li Shouzhen and Fu Yanqing to lead an army east against Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 光遠素無兵眾，惟嬰城自守，守貞以長連城圍之。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had never had many troops; he only held the city in defense while Shouzhen besieged it with an extended linked encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan had never had many troops; he could only hold the city and defend it while Shouzhen besieged him with a long linked encampment.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，承勛與弟承信、承祚見城中人民相食將盡，知事不濟，勸光遠乞降，冀免於赤族。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, Chengxun and his brothers Chengxin and Chengzuo saw the people in the city eating one another and near exhaustion; knowing the cause was lost, they urged Guangyuan to beg surrender, hoping to escape extermination of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Chengxun and his brothers Chengxin and Chengzuo saw the people in the city eating one another and near starvation; knowing the cause was lost, they urged Guangyuan to surrender, hoping to escape the extermination of the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 光遠不納，曰：「我在代北時，嘗以紙錢駝馬祭天池，皆沈沒，人言合有天子分，宜且待時，勿輕言降也。

translations.literal: Guangyuan would not accept and said: "When I was in Daibei I once sacrificed paper money, camels, and horses at the Heavenly Lake — all sank; people said I had the portion of a Son of Heaven; I should wait for the time and not lightly speak of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan refused and said, "When I was in Daibei I once sacrificed paper money, camels, and horses at the Heavenly Lake and they all sank; people said I had the portion of a Son of Heaven. I should wait for the right moment and not speak lightly of surrender.

sentences.zh: 」承勛慮禍在朝夕，與諸弟同謀，殺節度判官邱濤，親校杜延壽、楊瞻、白延祚等，梟其首，乃遣承祚送於守貞。

translations.literal: " Chengxun feared disaster was imminent; with his brothers he plotted to kill the military commissioner's aide Qiu Tao and the close officers Du Yanshou, Yang Zhan, Bai Yanzuo, and others, displayed their heads, and sent Chengzuo to Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengxun feared disaster was imminent; with his brothers he plotted to kill the military commissioner's aide Qiu Tao and the close officers Du Yanshou, Yang Zhan, Bai Yanzuo, and others, displayed their heads, and sent Chengzuo to Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 因縱火大噪，劫其父幽於私第，以城納款，遣即墨縣令王德柔貢表待罪，光遠亦上章自首。

translations.literal: They then set fires and raised a great uproar, seized their father and confined him in a private residence, surrendered the city, sent Jimo magistrate Wang Derou with a memorial accepting guilt, and Guangyuan also submitted a confession.
translations.idiomatic: They then set fires and raised a great uproar, seized their father and confined him in a private residence, surrendered the city, sent Jimo magistrate Wang Derou with a memorial accepting guilt, and Guangyuan also submitted a confession of his own.

sentences.zh: 少帝以頃歲太原歸命，欲曲全之，執政曰：「豈有逆狀滔天而赦之也？

translations.literal: The Last Emperor, recalling that Taiyuan had submitted a few years before, wished to spare him entirely; the chief ministers said: "How can treason filling heaven be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor, recalling that Taiyuan had submitted a few years before, wished to spare him; the chief ministers said, "How can treason filling heaven be pardoned?

sentences.zh: 」乃命守貞便宜處置。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Shouzhen to dispose of the matter as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 守貞遣人拉殺之，

translations.literal: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death,
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen sent men to strangle him to death,

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：守貞遣客省副使何延祚殺之於其家。

translations.literal: (Ouyang History: Shouzhen sent Chief of the Reception Bureau He Yanzuo to kill him at his home.
translations.idiomatic: (The Ouyang History records that Shouzhen sent Deputy Chief of the Reception Bureau He Yanzuo to kill him at his home.

sentences.zh: 以病卒聞。）〉

translations.literal: It was reported that he died of illness.)
translations.idiomatic: It was reported that he had died of illness.)

sentences.zh: 漢高祖即位，詔贈尚書令，追封齊王，仍令立碑。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and ordered a stele erected.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han took the throne, an edict posthumously made Guangyuan Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and ordered a stele erected.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其碑石無故自折，可知其陰責也。

translations.literal: Before long the stele stone broke in two for no apparent reason — one can infer the hidden guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the stele stone broke in two for no apparent reason — a sign of hidden guilt.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：楊光遠滅範延光之後，朝廷以其功高，授青州節度，封東平王，奄有登、萊、沂、密數郡。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: After Yang Guangyuan destroyed Fan Yanguang, the court because of his high merit made him military commissioner of Qingzhou and Prince of Dongping, holding Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records that after Yang Guangyuan destroyed Fan Yanguang, the court because of his great merit made him military commissioner of Qingzhou and Prince of Dongping, holding Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既而自負強盛，舉兵反，朝廷以宋州節度李守貞嘗與光遠有隙，乃命李討之。

translations.literal: Having grown proud of his strength he raised troops in rebellion; the court, because Songzhou military commissioner Li Shouzhen had once been at odds with Guangyuan, ordered Li to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Having grown proud of his strength, he raised troops in rebellion; the court, because Songzhou military commissioner Li Shouzhen had once been at odds with Guangyuan, ordered Li to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 李受詔欣然，志在必取，莫不身先矢石。

translations.literal: Li received the order with delight, determined to capture him, and all led from the front under arrow and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Li received the order with delight, determined to take him, and all led from the front under arrow and stone.

sentences.zh: 光遠見而懼之，度不能禦，遂降。

translations.literal: Guangyuan saw this and feared it; judging he could not resist, he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan saw this and was afraid; judging he could not resist, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，光遠反書至，中外大震，時百官起居次，忽有朝士揚言於眾曰：「楊光遠欲謀大事，吾不信也。

translations.literal: At first when Guangyuan's letter of rebellion arrived, court and countryside were greatly shaken; during the officials' audience, suddenly a court gentleman proclaimed to the crowd: "Yang Guangyuan intends a great enterprise — I do not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Guangyuan's letter of rebellion arrived, court and countryside were greatly shaken; during the officials' audience, suddenly a court gentleman proclaimed to the crowd, "Yang Guangyuan intends a great enterprise — I do not believe it.

sentences.zh: 光遠素患禿瘡，其妻又跛，自古豈有禿頭天子、跛腳皇后耶？

translations.literal: Guangyuan has always suffered from bald sores, and his wife is lame — since antiquity has there ever been a bald-headed emperor or a lame empress?
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan has always suffered from bald sores, and his wife is lame — since antiquity has there ever been a bald emperor or a lame empress?

sentences.zh: 」於是人心頓安，未幾，光遠果降。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon hearts were instantly calm; before long Guangyuan indeed surrendered.)
translations.idiomatic: " Hearts were instantly calmed; before long Guangyuan indeed surrendered.)

sentences.zh: 承勛，光遠之長子也。

translations.literal: Chengxun was Guangyuan's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun was Guangyuan's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 始名承貴，避少帝名改焉。

translations.literal: Originally named Chenggui; changed to avoid the Last Emperor's name.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Chenggui; the name was changed to avoid the Last Emperor's personal name.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭歷光、濮州刺史，光遠兼鎮河陽，命制置三城事。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he served as prefect of Guang and Pu; when Guangyuan concurrently governed Heyang, he was ordered to manage the three cities.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he served as prefect of Guang and Pu; when Guangyuan concurrently governed Heyang, he was ordered to manage affairs in the three cities.

sentences.zh: 光遠移鎮青州，授萊州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Guangyuan moved to Qingzhou, Chengxun was made defense commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyuan moved to Qingzhou, Chengxun was made defense commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡亦頗理，嘗憤父側之奸黨，欲殺之，每省父，父為匿焉。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he also governed fairly well; he once raged at the scheming faction beside his father and wished to kill them, but whenever he visited his father, his father hid them.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture he also governed fairly well; he once raged at the scheming faction around his father and wished to kill them, but whenever he visited his father, his father hid them.

sentences.zh: 及光遠構釁，嬰城以叛，承勛赴之，敵退，為王師所圍。

translations.literal: When Guangyuan incited trouble and held the city in rebellion, Chengxun went to join him; when the enemy withdrew, they were besieged by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyuan incited trouble and held the city in rebellion, Chengxun went to join him; when the enemy withdrew, they were besieged by the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 逾歲糧盡，與其弟承祚背父之命，出降王師，朝廷授汝州防禦使，尋改鄭州。

translations.literal: After more than a year when provisions were exhausted, he and his brother Chengzuo defied their father's orders and surrendered to the imperial army; the court made him defense commissioner of Ru and soon changed him to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, when provisions were exhausted, he and his brother Chengzuo defied their father's orders and surrendered to the imperial army; the court made him defense commissioner of Ru and soon transferred him to Zheng.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·楊承信傳》：光遠死，承信與弟承祚詣闕請死。

translations.literal: (Song History, biography of Yang Chengxin: After Guangyuan died, Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo came to court begging death.
translations.idiomatic: (The Song History, biography of Yang Chengxin, records that after Guangyuan died, Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo came to court begging to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，以承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍衛將軍，放歸，服喪私第，尋安置鄭州。）〉

translations.literal: An edict released them; Chengxin was made General of the Right Feathered Forest and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Cavalry; they were sent home to mourn at their private residence and soon settled at Zheng prefecture.)
translations.idiomatic: An edict released them; Chengxin was made General of the Right Feathered Forest and Chengzuo General of the Right Valiant Cavalry; they were sent home to mourn at their private residence and were soon settled at Zheng prefecture.)

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，遣騎士自圃田召至，責其害父背己，使臠其肉而殺之。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, they sent horsemen from Putian to summon him, blamed him for killing his father and betraying them, had his flesh sliced off, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans entered Bian, they sent horsemen from Putian to summon him, blamed him for killing his father and betraying them, had his flesh sliced off, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 以其弟承信為青州節度使。

translations.literal: His brother Chengxin was made military commissioner of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chengxin was made military commissioner of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 盧文進，字國用，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin, style name Guoyong, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenjin, whose style name was Guoyong, was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，飲啖過人，望之偉如也。

translations.literal: Seven feet tall, he ate and drank beyond ordinary men; seen from afar he looked imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Seven feet tall, he ate and drank more than other men; seen from afar he looked imposing.

sentences.zh: 少事劉守光為騎將，唐莊宗攻燕，以文進首降，遙授壽州刺史。

translations.literal: In youth he served Liu Shouguang as a cavalry commander; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong attacked Yan, Wenjin was the first to surrender and was appointed from afar as prefect of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Liu Shouguang as a cavalry commander; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong attacked Yan, Wenjin was the first to surrender and was appointed from afar as prefect of Shou.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗得山後八軍，以愛弟存矩為新州圍練使以總領之。

translations.literal: At first Zhuangzong obtained the eight armies behind the mountains and made his beloved younger brother Cunju regimental commissioner of Xin to command them overall.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhuangzong obtained the eight armies behind the mountains and made his beloved younger brother Cunju regimental commissioner of Xin to command them overall.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與劉鄩對壘於莘縣，命存矩於山後召募勁兵，又命山北居民出戰馬器仗，每鬻牛十頭易馬一匹，人心怨咨。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong faced Liu Yan at camp in Shen county and ordered Cunju to recruit elite troops behind the mountains; he also ordered the northern mountain residents to supply war horses and weapons — ten oxen traded for one horse — and resentment spread among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong faced Liu Yan in camp at Shen county and ordered Cunju to recruit elite troops behind the mountains; he also ordered the northern mountain residents to supply war horses and weapons — ten oxen for one horse — and resentment spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 時存矩團結五百騎，令文進將之，與存矩俱行。

translations.literal: At that time Cunju assembled five hundred horsemen, had Wenjin lead them, and traveled together with Cunju.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cunju assembled five hundred horsemen, had Wenjin lead them, and traveled together with Cunju.

sentences.zh: 至祁溝關，軍士聚謀曰：「我輩邊人，棄父母妻子，為他血戰，千里送死，固不能也。

translations.literal: Reaching Qigou Pass, the soldiers gathered and plotted: "We frontier men, abandoning parents, wives, and children to spill blood fighting for others — death sent a thousand li away — we truly cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Qigou Pass, the soldiers gathered and plotted, "We frontier men, abandoning parents, wives, and children to spill blood fighting for others — death sent a thousand li away — we truly cannot do it.

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「擁盧將軍卻還新州，據城自守，奈我何！

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "Let us make General Lu turn back to Xin, hold the city and defend ourselves — what can they do to us!
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd said, "Let us make General Lu turn back to Xin, hold the city, and defend ourselves — what can they do to us!

sentences.zh: 」因大呼揮戈，趣傳舍，害存矩於榻下。

translations.literal: " They then shouted, waved weapons, rushed to the relay station, and killed Cunju beneath his couch.
translations.idiomatic: " They then shouted, waved weapons, rushed to the relay station, and killed Cunju beneath his couch.

sentences.zh: 文進撫膺曰：「奴輩累我矣。

translations.literal: Wenjin clutched his chest and said: "You slaves have ruined me.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin clutched his chest and said, "You slaves have ruined me.

sentences.zh: 」因環屍而泣曰：「此輩既害郎君，我何面目見王！」

translations.literal: " He then circled the corpse weeping and said: "Since you wretches have killed the young lord, with what face can I see the prince!"
translations.idiomatic: " He then circled the corpse weeping and said, "Since you wretches have killed the young lord, with what face can I see the prince!"

sentences.zh: （案《遼史》：存矩取文進女為側室，文進心常內愧，因與亂軍殺存矩。）〉

translations.literal: (According to the Liao History: Cunju took Wenjin's daughter as a concubine; Wenjin was always inwardly ashamed, and together with the mutinous troops killed Cunju.)
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Liao History, Cunju took Wenjin's daughter as a concubine; Wenjin was always inwardly ashamed, and together with the mutinous troops killed Cunju.)

sentences.zh: 與薛史異因為亂軍所擁。

translations.literal: This differs from Xue's History — he was therefore taken up by the mutinous army.
translations.idiomatic: This differs from Xue's History — he was therefore taken up by the mutinous army.

sentences.zh: 反攻新州，不克；

translations.literal: He counterattacked Xin but could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: He counterattacked Xin but could not take it;

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：文進攻新州，不克，夜走墜塹，一躍而出，明日視之，乃郡之黑龍潭也，絕岸數丈，深不可測。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang: Wenjin attacked Xin but failed; fleeing by night he fell into a moat and leaped out in one bound; the next day he looked and saw it was the prefecture's Black Dragon Pool — cliffs several zhang high, depths unfathomable.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang records that Wenjin attacked Xin but failed; fleeing by night he fell into a moat and leaped out in one bound; the next day he looked and saw it was the prefecture's Black Dragon Pool — cliffs several zhang high and depths unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 又嘗有大蛇，徑至座間，引首及膝，文進取食飼之而去。

translations.literal: Again once a great serpent came straight to his seat, raised its head to his knee; Wenjin took food, fed it, and it departed.
translations.idiomatic: Again, once a great serpent came straight to his seat and raised its head to his knee; Wenjin took food, fed it, and it departed.

sentences.zh: 由是自負。）〉

translations.literal: From this he grew self-confident.)
translations.idiomatic: From this he grew self-confident.)

sentences.zh: 又攻武州，又不利。

translations.literal: He again attacked Wu prefecture and again failed.
translations.idiomatic: He again attacked Wu prefecture and again failed.

sentences.zh: 周德威命將追討，文進遂奔契丹，命為幽州兵馬留後，部分漢軍，常別為營寨。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei ordered generals to pursue; Wenjin then fled to the Khitans, was appointed rear commander of Youzhou's horse and troops, organized the Han armies, and always camped separately.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei ordered generals to pursue him; Wenjin then fled to the Khitans, was appointed rear commander of Youzhou's horse and troops, organized the Han armies, and always camped separately.

sentences.zh: 未幾，文進引契丹寇新州。

translations.literal: Before long Wenjin led Khitans to raid Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenjin led Khitans to raid Xin.

sentences.zh: 自是北師數至，驅擄數州士女，教其織纴工作，中國所為者悉備，契丹所以強盛者，得文進之故也。

translations.literal: From then on northern armies came repeatedly; they drove off and captured men and women of several prefectures, taught them weaving and crafts — everything done in China was fully available; that the Khitans grew strong was owing to obtaining Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on northern armies came repeatedly; they drove off and captured men and women of several prefectures and taught them weaving and crafts — everything done in China was fully available. That the Khitans grew strong was owing to obtaining Wenjin.

sentences.zh: （案《遼史》云：文進引契丹軍攻新州，刺史安金全不能守，棄城去。

translations.literal: (According to the 《Liao History》: Wenjin led Khitan armies to attack Xin prefecture; prefect An Jinquan could not hold it and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the 《Liao History》, Wenjin led Khitan armies against Xin; Prefect An Jinquan could not hold the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 周德威援之，進攻新州，契丹眾數萬，德威不勝，大敗奔歸。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei came to reinforce and advanced to attack Xin; Khitan forces numbered in the tens of thousands; Dewei could not prevail and was utterly defeated, fleeing back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei marched to relieve the city and attacked Xin, but Khitan forces numbered in the tens of thousands; Dewei was routed and fled back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 文進與契丹攻幽州，且二百日，城中圍困，晉王親將兵救之，方始解去。

translations.literal: Wenjin together with the Khitans attacked Youzhou for nearly two hundred days; the city was besieged; the Prince of Jin personally led troops to rescue it, and only then did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin and the Khitans besieged Youzhou for nearly two hundred days until the Prince of Jin led an army in person to raise the siege.

sentences.zh: 契丹以文進為幽州節度使，又以為盧龍節度使。）〉

translations.literal: The Khitans made Wenjin military commissioner of Youzhou and also made him military commissioner of Lulong.)
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans appointed Wenjin military commissioner of Youzhou and also of Lulong.)

sentences.zh: 同光之世，為患尤深。

translations.literal: In the era of Tongguang, the harm was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang era the damage he did was especially grave.

sentences.zh: 文進在平州，率奚族勁騎，鳥擊獸搏，倏來忽往，燕、趙諸州，荊榛滿目。

translations.literal: Wenjin was at Pingzhou, leading fierce cavalry of the Xi tribe; like birds striking and beasts grappling, they came suddenly and departed swiftly; in the prefectures of Yan and Zhao, thorns and brambles filled the eye.
translations.idiomatic: From Pingzhou Wenjin led fierce Xi horsemen who struck like hunting birds and beasts — appearing and vanishing in an instant — until thorns and ruin covered the lands of Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 軍屯涿州，每歲運糧，自瓦橋至幽州，勁兵猛將，援遞糧車，然猶為契丹所鈔，奔命不暇，皆文進導之也。

translations.literal: The army was encamped at Zhuo; each year grain was transported from Waqiao to Youzhou; elite troops and fierce generals escorted the relay grain carts — yet still they were raided by the Khitans, rushing about without respite — all of this Wenjin guided.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were stationed at Zhuo, and every year grain was hauled from Waqiao to Youzhou under escort of elite soldiers and fierce generals — yet the Khitans still cut off the convoys, and men raced to and fro without rest; Wenjin guided it all.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位之明年，文進自平州率所部十餘萬眾來奔。

translations.literal: The year after Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin from Pingzhou led his following of more than a hundred thousand to come and defect.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Mingzong took the throne, Wenjin led more than a hundred thousand followers from Pingzhou to defect.

sentences.zh: 行及幽州，先遣使上表曰：「頃以新州團練使李存矩，提衡郡邑，掌握恩威，虐黎庶則毒甚於豺狼，聚賦斂則貪盈於溝壑，人不堪命，士各離心，臣即拋父母之邦，入朔漠之地。

translations.literal: Reaching Youzhou, he first sent an envoy with a memorial stating: "Recently, as regimental commissioner of Xin, Li Cunju held the scales of the commandery and grasped both grace and wrath; in oppressing the common people his venom exceeded wolves and jackals; in gathering taxes and levies his greed overflowed ditches and ravines; the people could not endure their lot and officers each lost heart; your subject thereupon cast aside the land of his parents and entered the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Youzhou, he first sent an envoy with a memorial: "Of late the regimental commissioner of Xin, Li Cunju, held the scales of the commandery and wielded both favor and punishment; in oppressing the people he was more poisonous than wolves, and in gathering taxes his greed filled every ditch; the people could not bear their lot and the officers lost heart one by one — so your subject cast aside the land of his parents and entered the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 幾年雁塞，徒向日以傾心；

translations.literal: Several years at the wild-goose passes — in vain turning sunward to pour out my heart;
translations.idiomatic: Years at the wild-goose frontier, turning only toward the sun to pour out my heart in vain;

sentences.zh: 一望家山，每銷魂而斷目。

translations.literal: One gaze at home mountains — each time soul dissolving and sight breaking.
translations.idiomatic: One glimpse of home mountains — each time my soul withers and my sight fails.

sentences.zh: 李子卿之河畔，空有怨辭；

translations.literal: By the riverbank of Li Ziqing — only complaint in vain;
translations.idiomatic: Like Li Ziqing on the riverbank, I had only empty words of grievance;

sentences.zh: 石季倫之樂中，莫陳歸引。

translations.literal: Amid Shi Jilun's music — no chance to set forth the plea to return.
translations.idiomatic: like Shi Jilun amid his music, I could not even voice the plea to return home.

sentences.zh: 近聞皇帝陛下，皇天眷命，清明在躬，握紀乘乾，鼎新革故，始知大幸，有路朝宗，便貯歸心，祗伺良會。

translations.literal: Having lately heard that Your Majesty, Heaven's chosen, clarity and brightness in person, grasping the era and riding the sovereign hexagram, renewing the vessel and changing the old — I now know great fortune: there is a path to pay court at the capital; I have stored my heart of return and reverently await the good occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have heard that Your Majesty, Heaven's chosen, clear in virtue and bright in person, has grasped the age and mounted the sovereign hexagram, renewing all things and casting off the old — and I know my great fortune: there is a road back to the capital; I have kept my heart of return and reverently await the right moment.

sentences.zh: 臣十月十日，決計殺在城契丹，取十一日離州，押七八千車乘，領十五萬生靈，十四日已達幽州」云。
