translations.literal: Your subject on the tenth day of the tenth month resolved to kill the Khitans in the city; on the eleventh I departed the prefecture; escorting seven or eight thousand carts and leading a hundred and fifty thousand souls, on the fourteenth I had already reached Youzhou." — so it is recorded.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the tenth month your subject resolved to kill the Khitans in the city; on the eleventh I left the prefecture, escorting seven or eight thousand carts and leading a hundred and fifty thousand people; on the fourteenth I had already reached Youzhou." — so the memorial ran.

sentences.zh: 洎至洛陽，明宗寵待彌厚，授滑州節度使、檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, Mingzong favored and treated him ever more generously, appointing him military commissioner of Hua and honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang, Mingzong treated him with ever greater favor and made him military commissioner of Hua and honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移鎮鄧州，累加同平章事，入為上將軍。

translations.literal: After a year and more, he was transferred to garrison at Deng; was successively promoted to Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs; entered court as Upper General.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to Deng, promoted step by step to Co-Director of the Department of State Affairs, and entered court as Upper General.

sentences.zh: 長興中，復出鎮潞州，擒奸恤隱，甚獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: During Changxing, he again went out to garrison at Lu; capturing villains and showing compassion to the hidden — he gained great reputation at the time.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing he again took up the garrison at Lu, rooting out wrongdoers and showing mercy to the oppressed, and won great praise at the time.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，改安州節度使。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, he was changed to military commissioner of An.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was reassigned as military commissioner of An.

sentences.zh: 及高祖即位，與契丹敦好，文進以嘗背契丹，居不自安。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne and was on close terms with the Khitans, Wenjin, having once betrayed the Khitans, was ill at ease in his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne and renewed friendly ties with the Khitans, Wenjin — who had once betrayed them — could not feel secure in his post.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：文進居數鎮，頗有善政，兵民愛之。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: Wenjin held several garrisons and had quite good governance; soldiers and people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 records that Wenjin governed several garrisons with notable benevolence, and soldiers and civilians alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 其將行也，從數騎至營中，別其裨將李藏機，告以避契丹之意，將士皆拜為訣。）〉

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, with several horsemen he came to camp, took leave of his lieutenant Li Cangji, told him of his intent to avoid the Khitans; officers and soldiers all bowed in farewell.)
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to leave, he rode with a few followers into camp to bid farewell to his lieutenant Li Cangji and explain that he meant to escape the Khitans; officers and soldiers all bowed in parting.)

sentences.zh: 天福元年十二月，乃殺行軍司馬馮知兆、節度副使杜重貴等，率其部眾渡淮奔於金陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tianfu, he then killed marching army marshal Feng Zhizhao, deputy military commissioner Du Chonggui, and others, led his following across the Huai, and fled to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianfu 1 he killed the marching army marshal Feng Zhizhao, deputy military commissioner Du Chonggui, and others, then led his troops across the Huai and fled to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 李棨待之尤重，

translations.literal: Li Qi treated him with especial honor,
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi treated him with especial honor,

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》云：烈祖以文進為天雄統軍。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 states: Liezu made Wenjin commander of Tianxiong.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 states that Liezu appointed Wenjin commander of Tianxiong.)

sentences.zh: 偽命為宣州節度使，後卒於江南。

translations.literal: By false appointment he was made military commissioner of Xuan; later he died in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern regime appointed him military commissioner of Xuan, and he later died in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: （《金陵志》：文進自潤州召還，以左衛上將軍、兼中書令、范陽郡王奉朝請。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Jinling Gazetteer》: Wenjin was recalled from Runzhou and given the posts of Left Guard Upper General, concurrently Director of the Chancellery, and Prince of Fanyang attending court.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Jinling Gazetteer》 records that Wenjin was recalled from Runzhou and made Left Guard Upper General, concurrently Director of the Chancellery, and Prince of Fanyang attending court.)

sentences.zh: 李金全，本唐明宗之小豎也。

translations.literal: Li Jinquan was originally Mingzong of Tang's young attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinquan had originally been a young attendant in Mingzong of Tang's household.

sentences.zh: 其先出於吐谷渾。

translations.literal: His ancestors came from Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: His family traced its origins to Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 金全驍勇，善騎射，少從明宗征伐，以力戰有功，明宗即位，連典大郡。

translations.literal: Jinquan was fierce and brave, skilled at riding and archery; in youth he followed Mingzong on campaigns and, through hard fighting, achieved merit; when Mingzong took the throne, he successively administered great commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan was fierce and brave and skilled at riding and archery; from youth he followed Mingzong on campaign and won distinction in hard fighting; when Mingzong took the throne, he was put in charge of one great commandery after another.

sentences.zh: 天成中，授涇州節度使，在鎮數年，以掊斂為務。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, he was appointed military commissioner of Jing; garrisoning there several years, he made extortion his business.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of Jing, and for several years in his garrison he made extortion his chief occupation.

sentences.zh: 長興中，受代歸闕，始進馬數十匹，不數日又進之。

translations.literal: During Changxing, replaced and returned to court, he first presented several dozen horses; within a few days he presented again.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, after being replaced and recalled to court, he first presented several dozen horses, and within a few days presented again.

sentences.zh: 明宗召而謂之曰：「卿患馬多耶，何進貢之數也？

translations.literal: Mingzong summoned him and said: "Do you suffer from too many horses — why such repeated tribute?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong summoned him and said, "Do you have too many horses, that you keep sending them as tribute?

sentences.zh: 」又謂曰：「卿在涇州日，為理如何，無乃以馬為事否？

translations.literal: " Again he said: "In your days at Jing, how was your governance — could it be that horses were your chief concern?
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "When you were at Jing, how did you govern — was it not chiefly by trading in horses?

sentences.zh: 」金全慚謝而退。

translations.literal: " Jinquan withdrew in shame and apology.
translations.idiomatic: " Jinquan withdrew in shame and apology.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，授滄州節度使，累官至檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, summer, he was appointed military commissioner of Cang; by successive steps he reached Honorary Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he was appointed military commissioner of Cang, and by successive promotions reached Honorary Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，罷鎮歸闕，久留於京師。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, dismissed from his garrison and returned to court, he remained long in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he was removed from his garrison and recalled to court, where he remained for a long time.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之明年，安州屯將王暉殺節度使周瑰，詔遣金全以騎兵千人鎮撫其地。

translations.literal: The year after Gaozu took the throne, Wang Hui, garrison commander at An, killed military commissioner Zhou Gui; an edict dispatched Jinquan with a thousand cavalry to pacify and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Gaozu took the throne, Wang Hui, a garrison commander at An, killed Military Commissioner Zhou Gui; an edict sent Jinquan with a thousand cavalry to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 未及境，而暉為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Before reaching the border, Hui was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jinquan reached the border, Hui was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 金全至，亂軍數百人皆不安，金全說遣赴闕，密伏兵於野，盡殺之，又擒其軍校武彥和等數十人，斬之。

translations.literal: When Jinquan arrived, several hundred mutinous troops were all uneasy; Jinquan persuaded them to go to court, secretly laid ambush in the open country, and killed them all; he also captured several dozen of their army officers including Wu Yanhe and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinquan arrived, several hundred mutinous troops were all on edge; he persuaded them to go to court, then secretly set an ambush in the open country and killed them all; he also captured several dozen of their officers, including Wu Yanhe, and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 初，金全之將行也，高祖戒之曰：「王暉之亂，罪莫大焉，但慮封守不寧，則民受其弊。

translations.literal: At first, when Jinquan was about to depart, Gaozu admonished him: "Wang Hui's rebellion — the crime could not be greater; yet I fear that if the border garrison is unsettled, the people will suffer the harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinquan was about to set out, Gaozu warned him: "Wang Hui's rebellion was a crime without equal, yet if the border garrison is unsettled, the people will suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 」因折矢飛詔，約以不戮一人，仍許以暉為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then broke an arrow and sent a flying edict, pledging not to execute a single man, and still promised to make Hui prefect of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then broke an arrow and sent a flying edict, pledging that not a single man would be killed, and even promised to appoint Hui prefect of Tang.

sentences.zh: 又謂金全曰：「卿之此行，無失吾信。

translations.literal: Again he told Jinquan: "On this journey of yours, do not betray my trust.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Jinquan, "On this mission, do not betray my word.

sentences.zh: 」及金全至，聞彥和等當為亂之日，劫掠郡城，所獲財貨，悉在其第，遂殺而奪之。

translations.literal: " When Jinquan arrived, hearing that on the day Yanhe and the others had risen in mutiny they had plundered the commandery city and that all goods taken were in their residences, he killed them and seized the property.
translations.idiomatic: " When Jinquan arrived, he learned that on the day of the mutiny Yanhe and the others had plundered the commandery city and that the loot was all in their houses; he killed them and seized it.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：彥和且死，呼曰：「王暉首惡，天子猶赦之；

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: As Yanhe was about to die, he cried out: "Wang Hui was the chief villain — the Son of Heaven still pardoned him;
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》 records that as Yanhe was about to die, he cried out, "Wang Hui was the chief villain, and the Son of Heaven still pardoned him;

sentences.zh: 我輩脅從，何罪乎！」）〉

translations.literal: We were compelled to follow — what crime is ours!")
translations.idiomatic: we were compelled to follow — what crime is ours!")

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，以姑息金全故，不究其事，尋授以旄節。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of it; because he indulged Jinquan, he did not investigate the matter; soon he invested him with the staff and banner of command.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of it, he indulged Jinquan and did not pursue the matter; soon he invested him with the staff and banner of command.

sentences.zh: 金全有親吏胡漢筠者，勇譎嗇褊，貪詐殘忍，軍府之政，一以委之。

translations.literal: Jinquan had a personal clerk, Hu Hanyun, brave, crafty, miserly, and narrow; greedy, deceitful, and cruel — the garrison's government he wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan had a personal clerk named Hu Hanyun — brave, crafty, miserly, and narrow-minded, greedy, deceitful, and cruel — and he entrusted the whole government of the garrison to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞其事，遣吏賈仁紹往代其職，且召漢筠。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of these affairs and sent clerk Jia Renshao to replace him in his duties and also summon Hanyun.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard of this, he sent clerk Jia Renshao to replace Hanyun and summoned Hanyun to court.

sentences.zh: 漢筠內疚惶怖，金全乃列狀稱疾以聞。

translations.literal: Hanyun was inwardly guilty and terrified; Jinquan then submitted a memorial listing illness and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun was inwardly guilty and terrified; Jinquan then submitted a memorial claiming illness and reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 及仁紹至，漢筠鴆而殺之。

translations.literal: When Renshao arrived, Hanyun poisoned and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renshao arrived, Hanyun poisoned and killed him.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》：胡漢榮所為多不法，晉高祖患之，不欲因漢榮以累功臣，為選廉吏賈仁沼代之，且召漢榮。

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》: Hu Hanrong's conduct was largely unlawful; Later Jin's Gaozu was troubled by it and, not wishing to implicate a meritorious minister because of Hanrong, selected an upright clerk, Jia Renzhao, to replace him and also summon Hanrong.
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 records that Hu Hanrong's conduct was largely unlawful; Later Jin's Gaozu was troubled by it and, not wishing to ruin a meritorious minister because of Hanrong, chose the upright clerk Jia Renzhao to replace him and summoned Hanrong to court.

sentences.zh: 漢榮教金全留己而不遣。

translations.literal: Hanrong instructed Jinquan to keep him and not send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Hanrong urged Jinquan to keep him and refuse to send him away.

sentences.zh: 金全客龐令圖諫曰：「仁沼昔事王晏球，有大功，晏球欲厚賞之，仁沼退而不言，此天下之忠臣也。

translations.literal: Jinquan's guest Pang Lingtu remonstrated: "Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu and had great merit; Yanqiu wished to reward him generously — Renzhao withdrew and said nothing; this is a loyal minister under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan's guest Pang Lingtu remonstrated, "Renzhao once served Wang Yanqiu with great merit; when Yanqiu wished to reward him generously, Renzhao withdrew and said nothing — that is a loyal minister under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及頒賜所俘物，仁沼悉以分故人親戚之貧者，此天下之廉士也。

translations.literal: When distributed booty was awarded, Renzhao gave it all to old friends and poor relatives; this is an upright man under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When captured goods were distributed, Renzhao gave his share entirely to old friends and poor relatives — that is an upright man under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 宜納仁沼而遣漢榮。

translations.literal: You should accept Renzhao and send Hanrong away.
translations.idiomatic: You should accept Renzhao and send Hanrong away.

sentences.zh: 」漢榮聞之，夜使人殺令圖而鴆仁沼。）〉

translations.literal: " Hanrong heard of it; by night he sent men to kill Lingtu and poison Renzhao.)
translations.idiomatic: " When Hanrong heard of this, he sent men by night to kill Lingtu and poison Renzhao.)

sentences.zh: 天福五年夏，高祖命馬全節為安州節度使，以代金全。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu, Gaozu appointed Ma Quanjie military commissioner of An to replace Jinquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tianfu 5, Gaozu appointed Ma Quanjie military commissioner of An to replace Jinquan.

sentences.zh: 漢筠自以昔嘗拒命，復聞仁紹二子將訴置毒之事，居不自安，乃紿謂金全曰：「邸吏劉珂使健步倍道兼行，密傳其意，雲受代之後，朝廷將以仁紹之事詰公之罪。

translations.literal: Hanyun, thinking that he had once defied orders and hearing again that Renshao's two sons would sue over the poisoning affair, was ill at ease in his post; he then deceived Jinquan, saying: "Clerk Liu Ke sent a swift courier by forced march, secretly conveying his meaning, saying that after you accept replacement, the court will question your guilt over the Renshao affair.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyun, knowing he had once defied orders and hearing that Renshao's two sons would sue over the poisoning, could not feel secure; he deceived Jinquan, saying, "Clerk Liu Ke sent a swift courier by forced march with a secret message: once you accept replacement, the court will hold you to account for the Renshao affair.

sentences.zh: 」金全大駭，命從事張緯函表送款於淮夷。

translations.literal: " Jinquan was greatly terrified and ordered staff officer Zhang Wei to seal a memorial and send surrender to the Huai barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: " Jinquan was greatly alarmed and ordered his staff officer Zhang Wei to seal a memorial and send surrender to the Huai regime.

sentences.zh: 淮人遣偽將李承裕以代金全，金全即日南竄，其妓樂、車馬、珍奇、帑藏，皆為承裕所奪。

translations.literal: The Huai people sent the false general Li Chengyu to replace Jinquan; Jinquan that same day fled south; his courtesans, music, carriages, horses, rarities, and treasury stores were all seized by Chengyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai regime sent the general Li Chengyu to replace Jinquan; Jinquan fled south that same day, and Chengyu seized his courtesans, musicians, carriages, horses, rarities, and treasury stores.

sentences.zh: 與其黨數百人束身夜出，曉至氵義州，引領北望，泣下而去。

translations.literal: With several hundred of his faction, bound and bearing themselves, they went out by night; at dawn they reached Yi prefecture, turned their faces north, wept, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With several hundred followers he went out by night in bonds; at dawn they reached Yi prefecture, turned their faces north, wept, and went on.

sentences.zh: 及至金陵，李棨授以節鎮。

translations.literal: When he reached Jinling, Li Qi invested him with a commandery garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jinling, Li Qi invested him with a commandery garrison.

sentences.zh: （馬令《南唐書》云：烈祖以金全為天威統軍，遷潤州節度使。）〉

translations.literal: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 states: Liezu made Jinquan commander of Tianwei and transferred him to military commissioner of Run.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Ling's 《History of Southern Tang》 states that Liezu made Jinquan commander of Tianwei and transferred him to military commissioner of Run.)

sentences.zh: 後卒於江南。

translations.literal: Later he died in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：延光昔為唐臣，綽有令譽，洎逢晉祚，顯恣狂謀，既力屈以來降，尚顏而惜死，孟津之歿，乃取笑於千載也。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: Yanguang was once a minister of Tang and bore an excellent reputation; when he met the Jin mandate he openly indulged mad schemes; though his strength was broken and he came to surrender, he still clung to face and feared death — his death at Mengjin became a jest for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Yanguang was once a Tang minister of fine reputation; when the Jin dynasty arose he openly indulged reckless plots; though broken in strength and come to surrender, he still clung to face and feared death — and his end at Mengjin has been a laughingstock for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 從賓而下，俱怙亂以滅身，亦何足與議也。

translations.literal: From Congbin downward, all relied on rebellion to destroy themselves — what is there worth discussing?
translations.idiomatic: From Congbin downward, all relied on rebellion to destroy themselves — what is there worth discussing?

sentences.zh: 文進懼強敵之威，金全為輿臺所賣，事雖弗類，叛則攸同，鹹附島夷，皆可醜也。

translations.literal: Wenjin feared the might of a strong enemy; Jinquan was sold out by his own menials; though the cases differ, in rebellion they are the same — both attaching to the island barbarians, both equally shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin feared a powerful enemy; Jinquan was betrayed by his own servants; though their cases differ, in rebellion they are alike — both clinging to the island barbarians, and both are shameful.
